With the SKAO, we should push the explored parameter space further and in new directions in all of the sensitivity, field-of-view, time, spectral, spectro-dynamic, polarisation and imaging domains. We should utilise approaches such as machine learning in allowing us to address the complexity that arises from the expanded parameter space and increased data rates and candidate sources. We will briefly summarise some of the impressive progress that the SKA pathfinders and precursors have made in these areas and what these mean for the SKA telescopes. We will also discuss ways in which it might be possible to push the current capabilities.

papers.title: Quantum Broker: QoS-Aware Distribution of Quantum Computations
papers.abstract: Cloud-accessible quantum computing has made heterogeneous Quantum Processing Units (QPUs) available through provider platforms that differ in qubit technology, calibration state, queueing behavior, and pricing model. This heterogeneity makes execution management a quantum-engineering concern: a quantum circuit may be executable on several backends, but the resulting cost, latency, fidelity, and reproducibility depend on backend selection and on how measurement shots are allocated. This paper presents the Quantum Broker, an open-source and provider-agnostic framework for Quality-of-Service-aware quantum execution management. The framework operationalizes shot-wise distribution by exploiting the statistical independence of quantum measurement shots to dispatch a single circuit across multiple heterogeneous QPUs according to user-defined constraints and optimization objectives. It combines a modular execution architecture, interchangeable backend-profiling strategies, and the Quantum QoS Specification Language (QQSpec), a declarative language for expressing QoS requirements. Dispatch planning is supported by two solver backends: a mixed-integer linear-programming (MILP) solver, and a nonlinear dual-annealing solver. Experiments on benchmark quantum circuits and noisy simulator backends show that the Quantum Broker can produce feasible QoS-aware dispatch plans under heterogeneous backend conditions and can improve QoS satisfaction with respect to single-backend and naive multi-backend baselines. The results also expose a practical trade-off between planning time and dispatch quality, with the nonlinear solver producing higher-quality allocations at increased computational cost. Overall, the Quantum Broker provides an extensible execution-management layer for engineering portable, reproducible, and QoS-aware quantum software over fragmented quantum cloud infrastructures.

papers.title: Stabilizing Filters for Graph Signal Generation
papers.abstract: Generating graph signals is an important task in machine learning, and incorporating the underlying graph into a generative model enables structurally-informed distribution modeling. However, said graph is often noisy or imperfectly estimated, and structural errors can affect the generative process and the resulting signal distribution. While recent work has established stability guarantees for graph neural ordinary differential equations, the robustness of graph-aware reference dynamics, as used in topological Schrödinger bridge models, remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the structural stability of continuous-time generative models whose dynamics combine a graph filter with a learned graph neural network. We first derive a Wasserstein stability bound that quantifies the effect of graph perturbations on the generated signal distributions. Informed by this analysis, we then propose a principled framework for designing graph filters that balance structural stability with induced signal smoothing. We characterize the optimal filter design and provide an explicit family of polynomial filters with provable stability guarantees. Experiments on synthetic graphs and real-world fMRI signals support our theoretical findings, illustrating the enhanced structural stability of the proposed filters while preserving generative performance.

papers.title: Learning Normal Coordinates on Riemannian Manifolds with Flow Charts
papers.abstract: Riemannian manifolds are powerful models for problems with non-Euclidean structure. Recent work in geometric machine learning has focused on training deep neural networks to learn Riemannian metrics from high-dimensional data. However, many geometric algorithms require repeated evaluations of the exponential and logarithmic maps, whose high computational cost restricts the utility of learned Riemannian manifolds in practice. We propose to address this cost by training a conditional invertible neural network, called a flow chart, to approximate normal coordinates around points on a given Riemannian manifold. With this approach, the exponential and logarithmic maps can be approximated by fast Euclidean operations in the model's learned coordinate space. Our main contribution is an efficient loss function for training flow charts that is nonnegative and, under suitable domain assumptions, is zero precisely when the chart is normal. Across sixteen synthetic and data-derived geometries, flow charts are competitive with a specialized neural geodesic interpolator for logarithmic map estimation, while also being able to estimate the exponential map. When pretrained, flow charts provide a median speedup of 60-70x over numerical baselines at comparable logarithmic map estimation error, and their learned coordinates improve the accuracy of a numerical geodesic solver.

papers.title: SWatcher+: A Holistic Approach to Deploying Learned Cardinality Estimators in a Dynamic Setting
papers.abstract: Cardinality estimation (CE) is crucial in database query optimization. Although recent advances have improved accuracy, deploying machine-learned CE models in dynamic databases remains challenging due to data updates and workload shifts. Retraining can be costly, but existing practices offer little guidance on when and how to update models, resulting in simple periodic retaining strategies that are suboptimal. We propose SWatcher+, a framework that adapts learned CE to dynamic workloads by monitoring data updates and query feedback. SWatcher+ selectively monitors high-impact subqueries for which wrong estimates lead to poor plan performance, and it proactively applies corrections to estimates during query optimization. This strategy enables immediate adaption to data and workload shifts without waiting for full model retraining, and carefully balances the cost and benefit of monitoring and adaption versus retraining. Our experiments show that SWatcher+ offers a better trade-off between query performance and overhead compared with existing approaches, making it a more practical solution for deploying learned CE in dynamic settings.

papers.title: Dynamical Mean-Field Theory for Real Materials using Variational Quantum Compressed Time Evolution on a Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: We design a hybrid quantum-classical computational workflow, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory, to investigate the electronic properties of CaCuO2, a parent structure of high-temperature cuprate superconductors. Our approach uses a quantum algorithm as an impurity solver that is based on variational quantum compressed time evolution to compute the time-dependent Greens function on an IBM Heron quantum device. Utilizing error mitigation techniques and a Lehmann representation fitting procedure, we extract the density of states from the signal in the accessible time regime. Despite the significant challenges rooted in the residual imprecision of currently accessible NISQ devices, we successfully resolve the characteristic features of the spectral function. However, we find that the required numerical accuracy for full DMFT self-consistency exceeds current hardware capabilities, indicating that practical real-material DMFT applications will necessitate post-NISQ hardware developments.

papers.title: Norm-optimal model order reduction in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of model order reduction (MOR) in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs). We prove generalizations of well-known necessary interpolatory conditions for norm-optimal reduced-order models, originally stated for rational functions in $H_2$ Hardy-Hilbert spaces. We construct an alternative to the iterative rational Krylov (IRKA) algorithm for RKHSs with differentiable kernels to obtain norm-optimal reduced-order models. Then, we introduce generalized Malmquist-Takenaka (GMT) functions that can be used to define orthonormal bases in an arbitrary RKHS. Using GMT functions, we propose unitary transformations between separable RKHSs. This allows us to extend our optimality conditions and subsequent algorithms to MOR problems posed in RKHSs with non-differentiable kernels. The potential and versatility of the proposed MOR framework is demonstrated in several numerical experiments. We perform norm-optimal MOR on various machine learning models such as support vector machines and deep ReLU networks. In addition, we show how the proposed MOR framework can be used to solve seemingly unrelated problems. In particular, we provide an example for fitting high degree polynomials to data and also obtain a FEM-like method for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with an optimal kernel basis.

papers.title: Disentangling forced and internal components in observed climate evolution using spatiotemporal deep learning
papers.abstract: Attribution of observed historical climate evolution to externally forced change and internal variability is fundamental to understanding climate change and evaluating climate models. Yet such attribution remains challenging because the forced response is intertwined with internal variability in observations. Here, we develop a convolutional long short-term memory network (ConvLSTM) to disentangle these two components. Trained and evaluated using large-ensemble simulations from multiple climate models, ConvLSTM consistently outperforms existing model-based, statistical, and machine-learning approaches. Applying ConvLSTM to observations reveals an evolving spatial pattern of the forced response and substantial contributions from internal variability to recent multidecadal climate trends. For several key climate features whose attribution remains debated, ConvLSTM indicates that internal variability amplified the forced reversal of Atlantic interhemispheric temperature asymmetry, dominated the observed La Niña-like warming pattern over the equatorial Pacific and the associated precipitation decline over southwestern North America since 1980, and modulated Arctic amplification around its nearly constant threefold forced value. Comparison between the ConvLSTM-estimated and model-simulated forced responses reveals broadly consistent patterns but also important discrepancies, with climate models simulating stronger Northern Hemisphere warming, weaker subtropical high intensification, and smaller land precipitation declines. Overall, ConvLSTM provides a robust framework for attributing historical climate evolution and evaluating the fidelity of climate models

papers.title: Structured light for addressable two-qubit gates in medium-sized ion crystals: modeling motional and dephasing errors
papers.abstract: Geometric phase gates with addressed laser radiation are widely used in trapped-ion quantum computers to drive high-fidelity entangling gates on an arbitrary qubit pair of a larger ion chain. Such programmable connectivity exploits the collective phonons to mediate the desired interaction, while simultaneously achieving robustness to their thermal fluctuations by a careful calibration of the gate time with respect to the laser and vibrational-mode frequencies. Crosstalk errors can arise when the spectator qubits, which should ideally remain idle during the gate, are partially driven by the laser fields. The minimal crosstalk, which is set by the laser beam size on the spectator ions, can be achieved when the addressing beams propagate perpendicular to the ion chain. However, this results in exciting the radial phonons, and can complicate achieving high-fidelities as the ion chain grows due to the so-called spectral mode crowding. In this work, we present the theoretical description of a scheme recently implemented by Faorlin et $al.$. This scheme overcomes these complications by engineering addressable state-dependent forces along the ion-chain with laser beams that propagate perpendicular to it through the use of structured light gradients. In this way, one can excite the axial phonons and avoid the spectral mode crowding, while simultaneously minimizing the crosstalk. We present a detailed derivation of the entangling gate scheme, together with analytical closed-form expressions for the leading contribution to the gate error caused by thermal motional fluctuations and dephasing noise. Our results confirm that such fluctuations account for up to 93$\%$ of the error budget under the operating conditions of the gate implemented by Faorlin et $al.$. We identify target parameters to reduce the motional error from the reported $10^{-3}$ to the $10^{-5}$ level.

papers.title: Scalable Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization: A Super-resolution and Simultaneous Approach Based on Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Large-scale topology optimization (TO) remains computationally demanding, especially for stress-constrained problems. To address this challenge, we propose the simultaneous neural topology optimization (SNTO) framework where we represent state, adjoint, and design variables with custom neural networks (NNs) whose parameters are jointly optimized within a single optimization loop that leverages continuous adjoint analysis and automatic differentiation. This optimization minimizes a multi-component loss function that combines the design objective, an aggregation of the local stress constraints, and the potential energy functionals. Our NNs have a unique architecture that accelerates convergence while enabling the networks to capture sharp gradients and boundaries which are critical to stress-constrained TO. To achieve scalability to millions of degrees of freedom (DoF), we develop a hardware-aware training scheme in which the design domain is partitioned into subdomains that are distributed across multiple GPUs. To control peak GPU memory usage, we further slice each subdomain into smaller regions whose loss gradients are evaluated sequentially and accumulated to update the NN parameters. Unlike domain decomposition approaches, our partitioning naturally ensures field continuity across the subdomains and does not require the introduction of additional terms into the loss function. For validation, we first evaluate the proposed framework on various 2D stress-constrained benchmarks and compare our results to a conventional finite element-based approach, showing that SNTO produces super-resolution designs with sharper boundaries, smaller gray areas, and lower volume fractions. We then consider large-scale 3D problems with up to eight million collocation points and distribute the training over up to eight GPUs.

papers.title: IECG: Weakly-Supervised Interpretability-Enhancing Foundation Model for Electrocardiogram
papers.abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is a cornerstone of cardiac diagnosis, yet most machine learning methods for ECG analysis lack interpretability, limiting their clinical adoption. We present IECG, a weakly-supervised ECG foundation model that jointly performs diagnostic classification and abnormality localization without requiring manual abnormal region annotations, overcoming a long-standing bottleneck in interpretable ECG learning. Central to IECG is a weakly-supervised attention strategy that explicitly incorporates clinical priors by deriving abnormality heatmap pseudo-labels from established ECG clinical knowledge. These pseudo-labels guide the model's CLS-token attention through a KL-divergence loss, encouraging it to focus on diagnostically relevant waveform regions. During pretraining, IECG is jointly optimized with clinically guided attention supervision, ECG-text contrastive alignment, and report captioning objectives, enabling it to learn rich multimodal representations while producing localized waveform evidence. By explicitly aggregating features from clinically guided attention regions, IECG grounds its diagnostic predictions in interpretable waveform evidence without sacrificing classification performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that IECG achieves state-of-the-art abnormal region localization while maintaining strong classification performance, advancing trustworthy foundation models for ECG analysis.

papers.title: A Process-Informed, Photorealistic Digital Twin for Vision-Based Inline Inspection of C-SMC Strip Deposition
papers.abstract: Inline quality assurance for Sheet Molding Compound (SMC) manufacturing is hindered by the lack of large-scale, accurately labeled image datasets for training machine-learning models. This work presents a process-informed, photorealistic digital twin for carbon-fiber SMC strip deposition. A rigid-body simulation reproduces the deposition kinematics (settling, friction, belt motion), while a physically grounded polarization-rendering model produces realistic appearance, so that every image carries exact, mutually consistent labels in synchronized formats: oriented bounding boxes, point annotations, density maps, and polarization renderings (Angle and Degree of Linear Polarization). Because the joint distribution of many overlapping strips cannot be specified analytically, simulation yields exact, scalable ground truth that manual annotation cannot provide. The twin produces over 16,000 images across 3,300 frames, and the synthetic data replicate near-isotropic fiber orientation (axial concentration r < 0.05) consistent with as-deposited commercial SMC. Trained purely on synthetic data, YOLOv11 and CSRNet reach detection mAP50 up to 0.91, with a dedicated oriented-bounding-box detector confirming the oriented labels are directly trainable (mAP50 = 0.83); on real manufacturing images, the synthetic-to-real difference in edge and texture structure (Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance 0.46, distribution overlap 0.56) is of the same magnitude as the difference between two real acquisition series of the same material (0.41, overlap 0.57). The approach substantially reduces the labeling burden for camera-based inline inspection of fiber orientation and volume content.

papers.title: When Does Training on Synthetic Data Provably Work?
papers.abstract: High-quality training data are a major bottleneck in machine learning, motivating increasing use of artificially generated data. We study when a binary classifier trained on synthetic data transfers successfully to a real distribution, under a shared conditional label distribution. First, we derive finite-sample excess-error bounds when the real covariate distribution is absolutely continuous with respect to the synthetic distribution under a controlled density ratio. Second, we study the partially and fully singular case, where the real distribution has mass outside the synthetic one. If the hypothesis class is sufficiently expressive, synthetic risk alone cannot uniformly control real-world error: a classifier can be nearly optimal on synthetic data while approaching worst-case error on the uncovered real region, even when the distributions are arbitrarily close in Wasserstein distance. For function classes where hypotheses and the log-odds of the conditional label probability are Lipschitz, we recover a bound in terms of the probability that a real sample lies outside the reach of the synthetic data, restoring a transfer guarantee even in the fully singular case. Experiments confirm this in controlled low-dimensional settings and on 32,200 images generated as counterparts to real ImageNet images by four state-of-the-art generators: an adversarial classifier reaches 0.5% error on the synthetic domain but 99.25% error on the real domain, while ordinarily trained architectures show positively correlated synthetic and real test errors. Synthetic data should be budgeted at high sample counts and models validated on real data.

papers.title: On Johnson-Lindenstrauss Transforms for Byzantine-Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: The growing scale of data and models in machine learning calls for efficient optimization methods. Distributed optimization addresses this challenge, with compression mechanisms helping to reduce communication costs. A classical tool for dimensionality reduction is the Johnson-Lindenstrauss (JL) transform, which is simple to implement and offers strong geometric guarantees. In particular, JL transforms approximately preserve inner products and pairwise distances between vectors with high probability. In this paper, we exploit this property in Byzantine-robust optimization, where worker messages are weighted according to their alignment with a trusted reference gradient. We further support our theoretical findings with experimental results.

papers.title: Understanding Data Augmentation under Label Noise
papers.abstract: Data augmentation (DA) has become a fundamental component of modern machine learning systems and is widely regarded as an effective strategy for improving robustness and generalization. Despite its empirical success, the theoretical impact of DA under label noise remains poorly understood. In this work, we first theoretically explain when DA is beneficial and when it becomes detrimental, and provide sufficient conditions for distinguishing between these two regimes under both the i.i.d. learning setting and the more challenging domain generalization scenario. Then, we reveal a counterintuitive phenomenon: DA essentially acts as an uncertainty amplifier in the learning process, decreasing model stability and generalization performance. This finding is supported by the proposed learning and generalization bounds. Our analyses do not depend on specific DA techniques and require only mild assumptions, indicating that the results are applicable to a broad range of machine learning scenarios. Namely, we provide a unified theoretical foundation for understanding, analyzing, and designing DA methods in the presence of label noise.

papers.title: CyberHull: Deterministic Malicious URL Isolation via Convex Hull
papers.abstract: The emergence of increasingly sophisticated and evasion-resistant phishing attack strategies represents a significant threat to modern cybersecurity, particularly in cyber-physical systems and internet-based networks. Traditional probabilistic methods and certain machine learning approaches often struggle to detect novel attacks and may lack interpretability or portability. To address these challenges, we introduce CyberHull, a resource-efficient and deterministic framework for identifying malicious URLs through mathematically defined convex hull boundaries across multiple orthogonal feature domains, including structural content entropy, hyperlink graph topology, and semantic token distribution. CyberHull constructs compact convex hulls, referred to as vaults, using the QuickHull algorithm, with a training complexity of O(n log n) under suitable assumptions. URL classification is performed through point-in-polyhedron tests that impose relatively low computational overhead on standard CPUs. Experimental results demonstrate that CyberHull achieves 92 percent detection accuracy, substantially outperforming a baseline linear approach based on Principal Component Analysis (PCA), which achieves 32 percent accuracy. Furthermore, CyberHull offers a computationally efficient alternative to resource-intensive deep learning approaches for malicious URL detection.

papers.title: Learning the open string spectrum with neural networks
papers.abstract: The tree-level open superstring has an integer mass-squared spectrum on linear Regge trajectories. To what extent is this fixed by consistency conditions: locality, analyticity, crossing, unitarity together with the requirement that $2\to2$ scattering minimize the entanglement it generates? Using the local two-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity ($λ$-CSDR) we set up a bootstrap treating both the mass-squared spectrum and the partial-wave coefficients as unknowns which lets the machine learning algorithm to learn the mass-squared spectrum and partial-wave coefficients simultaneously, going beyond earlier work in which the spectrum was fixed. Using the local three-channel crossing symmetric dispersion relation with one-parameter ambiguity we obtain, within the class of amplitudes with soft Regge behavior and infinite higher-spin tower, a bound on the leading Wilson coefficients that we compare with existing bounds and trace to spin-0 dominance. We locate the Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude in the allowed region of the Wilson coefficients space. For amplitudes with two-channel crossing symmetry we find that a Non-dual amplitude exhibits a Polchinski-Strassler type transition from Regge to power-law behavior.

papers.title: Exploring Recurrent-Depth Language Models for Multitask Clinical Text Processing
papers.abstract: Clinical natural language processing includes diverse tasks such as information extraction, classification, and question answering. Developing one model for all tasks could simplify deployment and improve knowledge transfer. We evaluated whether small recurrent-depth language models can meet this need through joint fine-tuning and compared their performance with standard transformers. We fine-tuned Ouro1.4B-Thinking, Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, HRM-Text-1B, Qwen3-1.7B, and Qwen3-8B on 9 datasets covering information extraction, classification, inference, and question answering, and evaluated them on four additional datasets excluded from training. Across these 13 datasets, Ouro-1.4B-Thinking achieved higher performances than Qwen3-1.7B on 11 datasets; Ouro-2.6BThinking was competitive with Qwen3-8B on most tasks. Ouro models showed the largest gains on inference and question answering, whereas HRM-Text-1B showed mixed results. These findings support further study of recurrent-depth models for clinical tasks through controlled experiments to isolate architectural effects and investigate how recurrent computation influences reasoning, knowledge acquisition, and generalization.

papers.title: Adversarial Benchmarks and BenchDoor Attacks: Exploiting Benchmark Incentives for Backdoor Attacks
papers.abstract: Machine learning benchmarks act as guideposts for model development and spur the creation of training datasets intended to improve benchmark scores. We introduce BenchDoor, a family of data poisoning attacks that exploits this incentive. Beyond preserving benign performance, BenchDoor requires benchmark gains that encourage adoption of data that also implants a backdoor. The adversary either manipulates a benchmark's training or test data, creating an adversarial benchmark, or supplies an independent training dataset while leaving the benchmark unchanged. We formalize five attack scenarios, including training on rewritten test examples and applying similarity-based decontamination. Across multiple-choice Q&A, text classification, and open-ended Q&A with Qwen and Gemma models, BenchDoor achieves positive benchmark gains for all 30 evaluated configurations, with held-out attack success rates of 82.33% to 100.00% at poisoning rates of 2% to 10%. Both objectives remain achievable after synthetic data generation and similarity-based decontamination, with attack success rates of at least 90.33%. These findings show how benchmarks can serve as attack vectors both through their own data and through training resources that deliver improvements on them.

papers.title: ZKPU: Zero-Knowledge Processing Unit for Heterogeneous Workloads
papers.abstract: Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) have become a fundamental building block for privacy-preserving computation, blockchain systems, and verifiable machine learning. Modern ZKP protocols span two distinct families: curve-based protocols, which rely on large finite-field arithmetic, and hash-based protocols, which operate over native 64-bit fields. Existing hardware accelerators are specialized for one protocol family because they are built on operand-scanning Montgomery multiplication, resulting in fixed-width datapaths, poor utilization across heterogeneous operand widths, and limited scalability.   This paper presents \emph{ZKPU}, a Zero-Knowledge Processing Unit for heterogeneous ZKP workloads. ZKPU introduces a new compute paradigm by co-designing finely integrated product scanning (FIPS) Montgomery multiplication with a reconfigurable Twin Systolic Fabric (TSF), enabling modular multiplication at arbitrary widths in 64-bit increments. Combined with a fine-grained Deque buffer, on-chip twiddle-factor generator, and memory-efficient MSM preprocessing strategy, ZKPU provides a unified architecture for both curve-based and hash-based protocols. Evaluation using Groth16 and Plonky2 shows that ZKPU achieves up to $144\times$ speedup for NTT, $13.6\times$ for MSM, and approximately $7.2\times$ end-to-end application speedup over state-of-the-art accelerators, while being the first architecture to efficiently support both protocol families on a single reconfigurable hardware platform.

papers.title: Quantum Cryptanalysis on Two Feistel-Type Constructions
papers.abstract: With the rapid advancement of quantum computing, the security of traditional cryptographic systems is facing significant challenges. As a fundamental component of symmetric cryptography, block ciphers have attracted increasing attention regarding their quantum security in recent years.   In this paper, we propose new quantum attacks on two Feistel-type constructions, i.e., New Structure IV and the lightweight block cipher LBlock, under the quantum chosen-plaintext attack (qCPA) model. First, we construct an 8-round quantum distinguisher for New Structure IV and perform an $r(r>12)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. Compared with Li et al.'s qCPA-based result presented at INSCRYPT 2024, our attack reduces the time complexity by a factor of $2^{n/2}$, where $n$ denotes the subkey length. Second, we design a 9-round quantum distinguisher for LBlock and extend it to an $r(r>15)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. The proposed quantum distinguisher covers one more round than Liu et al.'s automated-search distinguisher at ASIACRYPT 2025, which results in a $2^{16}$ reduction in the time complexity of our $r$-round quantum key-recovery attack on LBlock. Furthermore, by analyzing the structure of the round function and the key scheduling of LBlock, we reduce the subkey guess space for the 15-round attack from 76 bits to 52 bits, lowering the time complexity from \(O(2^{38})\) to \(O(2^{26})\) by a factor of \(2^{12}\).

papers.title: Securing Agentic Commerce Through Behavior-Aware Fraud Detection and Cybersecurity for Trusted AI-Agent Payment Authorization
papers.abstract: The growing use of autonomous artificial intelligence agents in digital commerce creates new security concerns involving agent impersonation, unauthorized payments, compromised agents, and misuse of delegated authority. This research introduces the Autonomous Commerce Agent Guard System (ACAGS), a cybersecurity framework combining supervised machine learning, behavioral analytics, agent-specific authorization controls, and explainable AI. The framework was evaluated using synthetic financial transaction data augmented with simulated agent characteristics and five adversarial scenarios. XGBoost was selected following comparisons with alternative classifiers. Across ten experimental runs, behavioral features improved mean F1-score from 52.12% to 67.49%, with agent-specific features increasing performance to 69.46%. The framework achieved detection rates of 99.77% for abnormal agent behavior, 99.73% for impersonation, and 100% for malicious delegation and authorization-scope violations. Compromised-agent detection reached 72.27%. ACAGS also supported APPROVE, REVIEW, and REJECT authorization outcomes, with SHAP explanations providing model interpretability. The results demonstrate the potential of combining behavioral intelligence and delegated authorization controls to strengthen simulated agentic-commerce payment security, while highlighting the need for validation using real-world transactions.

papers.title: Privacy-Preserving Personalized Federated Learning (PPP-FL) for Medical Imaging
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm that reduces transmission costs, mitigates cross-border data sharing restrictions, and enhances privacy by keeping raw data on local devices. Clients in FL systems train local models and share only updates, which are aggregated by a central server. While this setup limits direct data exposure, FL remains vulnerable to privacy attacks. Existing attack and defense strategies have largely been developed for centralized systems, and adapting them to FL introduces new challenges due to its unique architecture and training workflow. In this work, we first propose a model inversion attack on FL systems using Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGANs) in the context of large-scale medical imaging. Our method operates under realistic assumptions about the attacker's knowledge and capabilities. We then examine the effect of client-side differential privacy (DP) in mitigating privacy leakage and incorporate personalized FL to improve model performance under DP settings. Experiments on the Brain MRI ND-5 dataset show that DCGAN-based attacks can reconstruct semantically meaningful synthetic images, revealing significant risks to the privacy of training data. Applying DP reduces attack success but introduces an accuracy trade-off, which is further overcome by personalized FL at each client side. We also evaluate how different aggregation algorithms affect both attack vulnerability and defense effectiveness, underscoring the critical role of aggregation strategies. The proposed attack-and-defense framework is model-agnostic and applicable to a wide range of FL-based systems.

papers.title: Interflow: Breaking the Offline-Online Barrier for Private AI at the Edge
papers.abstract: Privacy-preserving machine learning (PPML) offers a promising path toward bringing powerful AI services to the edge without exposing sensitive user data. However, its practical deployment remains constrained by the high communication, computation, and data-movement costs of secure multi-party computation (MPC), particularly during nonlinear inference. Existing MPC systems typically decouple input-independent correlated randomness generation from online execution, creating substantial memory pressure to buffer single-use cryptographic data. Moreover, limited storage can force a stop-and-refill execution pattern that repeatedly stalls the pipeline to replenish these buffers, bringing randomness generation back onto the critical path. We propose Interflow, an algorithm-hardware co-design that rethinks this separation by batch-wise processing and pipelining correlated-randomness generation with online execution: while the current batch consumes pre-generated randomness to execute secure nonlinear operations, correlation generation proceeds concurrently for the next batch. By leveraging interleaved execution, efficient data movement, and hardware acceleration, the design transforms preprocessing from a serialized, storage-intensive offline phase into a continuously overlapped pipeline that generates correlated randomness closer to the point of consumption, reducing memory footprint and data movement overhead. Implemented on the Zynq UltraScale+ ZCU102, Interflow improves nonlinear evaluation throughput by up to 1.55x for CNN operators and 1.48x for transformer operators. It achieves up to 1.26x speedup for ResNet-50 and up to 1.21x speedup for BERT-base, and reduces memory footprint by up to 37%, compared with baseline frameworks.

papers.title: A Bayesian machine learning approach to direct and spillover effects in cluster-randomized trials with noncompliance
papers.abstract: We develop a Bayesian machine learning approach for estimating direct and spillover effects in cluster-randomized trials with treatment noncompliance. To flexibly model outcomes and treatment receipt while accounting for within-cluster dependence, we combine Bayesian additive regression trees with cluster-level random effects. We augment the outcome regression with a peer-treatment clever covariate, defined as the predicted mean proportion of treated peers from a preliminary receipt model, to mitigate regularization-induced distortion of the effect decomposition. Within a Bayesian g-computation framework, we estimate cluster-average intent-to-treat effects and cluster-average local average treatment effects and examine sensitivity to the cross-world restrictions underlying their decomposition. Simulation studies show reduced bias under model misspecification, while the correctly specified parametric models show expected frequentist properties. We find that the clever covariate improves the decomposition of the total effect into direct and spillover components under moderate or strong spillover, with similar gains in smaller clusters. Its benefits vary with spillover strength, and the $95\%$ credible intervals remain conservative. An application to the Primary School Deworming Project in Kenya suggests reduced infection risk, with a larger estimated contribution from individual treatment receipt than from peer receipt. Overall, our approach provides a flexible Bayesian estimation of direct and spillover effect decomposition in the presence of treatment noncompliance.

papers.title: Quantum algorithm for high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equations based on Carleman linearization
papers.abstract: Addressing nonlinear numerical problems in quantum computing remains challenging, but several approaches, including Carleman linearization (CL), have been proposed to construct quantum algorithms for such problems. In this work, we develop a CL-based method for a high-dimensional nonlinear stochastic differential equation (SDE) $\mathrm{d} \mathbf{X}_t = \left(A(t) \mathbf{X}_t + F(t) \mathbf{X}_t^{\otimes s}\right) \mathrm{d} t + B(t) \mathrm{d} \mathbf{W}_t$ for an $\mathbb{R}^N$-valued random process $\mathbf{X}_t$, aiming at quantum speed-up with respect to the dimension $N$. We introduce auxiliary processes $\mathbf{Y}^j_t$ that approximate $\mathbf{X}_t^{\otimes j}$, derive a linearized system of SDEs for them, and obtain the linear ordinary differential equation (ODE) governing their expectations. We then apply a quantum ODE solver to it and, from the resulting quantum state, extract an estimate for the expectation of a linear function of $\mathbf{X}_t$ by overlap estimation. We show that, provided the nonlinear and noise terms in the SDE are sufficiently small relative to the linear term, the CL error decreases exponentially with the truncation order $J$ in CL, and we can estimate the target expectation with a ${\rm polylog}(N)$ number of queries to unitaries encoding coefficient matrices $A$, $F$, and $B$. Finally, we also run a numerical demonstration for an SDE related to Langevin dynamics, observing the exponential decay of the CL error as $J$ increases.

papers.title: Communication Complexity of Universal Features
papers.abstract: Motivated by the notion of features from machine learning, we study the complexity of representing data that allows for evaluation with a given family of functions. Concretely, we consider a deterministic encoder that observes $X\sim D$ and produces a finite encoding before a task $f\in\mathcal{F}\subseteq\{0,1\}^{\mathcal{X}}$ is specified. For each task, a decoder must predict $f(X)$ with error at most $\varepsilon$ under $D$. We construct an encoder that outputs a representation with $O(d^{*}\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bits, where $d^{*}$ is the dual VC dimension of $\mathcal{F}$. Our encoder greedily selects $O((d^{*}/\varepsilon)\log(1/\varepsilon))$ functions from the class and uses their joint label pattern to produce the encoding. The key idea in our upper bound is a novel potential function argument, where we compare the entropy gained from each greedy selection with the number of patterns allowed by the dual VC dimension. We present lower bounds showing that the representation length achieved by our encoder is worst-case optimal for every $d^* \ge 1$ and $\varepsilon < 1/4$ up to a universal constant factor, and instance-wise optimal for every family $\mathcal{F}$ up to an $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ factor. We give two ways to learn the representation from unlabeled samples, with different guarantees on the representation size and sample complexity. Experimentally, we verify the greedy construction's accuracy-size tradeoff and explore its connection to neural sparse autoencoders.

papers.title: Fixed-Size Active Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: Variance reduction techniques improve the efficiency of drawing conclusions from data. Recent proposals for variance-reduction use two complementary techniques to reduce variance: incorporating machine learning predictions into estimators and weighted sampling. A popular weighted sampling algorithm is Poisson Sampling (PS), which independently flips a biased coin at each unit and includes all heads in the sample. A fundamental flaw with PS is that it has a random sample size, which presents practical challenges and introduces variance into the estimator. We show that a fixed-size alternative, known in survey sampling as Conditional Poisson Sampling (CPS), is a drop-in replacement for PS on general multivariate Z-estimation problems, which include convex M-estimation considered in prior work. Notably, we show that the asymptotic variance of CPS is no worse than that of PS, and can be substantially better in realistic scenarios where predictions are imperfect. We illustrate these advantages on both synthetic and real datasets, and release a Python package implementing CPS. In light of our contributions, there is no need to suffer a variable sample size.

papers.title: Conversational AI for Perceived Cognitive Decline Screening in Older Adults
papers.abstract: Early detection of cognitive decline in older adults remains challenging due to the resource demands of standard neuropsychological assessments. Chatbot-based Intelligent Cognitive Assistants (ICAs) provide a scalable alternative by eliciting open-ended responses rich in linguistic, semantic, and autobiographical cues. This study evaluates whether ICA question-answer (Q/A) interviews with older adults can screen for participant-reported perceived cognitive decline and related cognitive, functional, and personality outcomes. We compare traditional machine learning, frozen transformer embeddings, fine-tuned transformers, and large language model (LLM) reasoning strategies across Global Q/A, Single Q/A confidence averaging, and Aggregated Q/A pipelines. Among text-based methods, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite (1-example-per-class, Aggregated Q/A) achieved the highest held-out test performance (0.742 accuracy, 0.739 balanced accuracy, 0.728 macro-F1). Given the small test set (n = 31), these results are interpreted descriptively. Frozen clinical transformer embeddings with a random forest head led non-LLM text methods, whereas fine-tuned models showed limited generalization. Models utilizing structured questionnaires, cognitive tasks, and personality traits outperformed text-based models in classification. Continuous regression analyses revealed modest predictive signals for AD8, FAQ, IQCODE, neuroticism, and conscientiousness. Exploratory prompt-level analyses identified both direct symptom-related and indirect autobiographical questions with strong test metrics, though sample sizes varied across prompts. These findings indicate that ICA chatbot interviews capture meaningful signals of perceived cognitive decline, supporting scalable screening research. Larger, clinically diverse cohorts with validated clinical outcomes are needed for clinical translation.

papers.title: Machine-learned spectral PDE solvers for fluids and plasmas
papers.abstract: Sparse regression methods for discovering governing partial differential equations (PDEs) from data are sensitive to observation noise and are not constrained to reproduce the data under forward integration. We address both limitations by performing weak-form discovery in the spatial discretization in which the PDE is solved, learned by differentiating through multistep rollouts anchored at the observed states. The new method, Weak-form Anchored Rollout for PDEs (WARP), produces a machine-learned PDE solver. In this work, we focus on systems amenable to a spectral Galerkin solver. Across eight benchmark fluid and plasma systems, including high-dimensional turbulent simulations, WARP produces numerically stable rollouts from new random initial conditions and substantially improves coefficient recovery, rollout accuracy, and statistical measures compared with a single-step weak-form SINDy baseline.

papers.title: J-PLUS: Identifying Outlier Spectral Energy Distributions in the Fourth Data Release Using Unsupervised Machine Learning
papers.abstract: The selection of candidates belonging to rare or underrepresented stellar populations, as well as novel objects, is essential for spectroscopic follow-up. In this work, we demonstrate how combining broad- and narrow-band photometric information with machine-learning techniques enables this selection. Using photometric data in twelve filters from the Javalambre Photometric Local Universe Survey (J-PLUS) as input, we applied an anomaly detection technique based on autoencoders to identify spectral energy distributions (SEDs) that deviate from the dominant pattern in the J-PLUS objects sample. Subsequently, we applied the t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) algorithm to the J-PLUS colors of the outlier SEDs population. Combining information from the SIMBAD database and other astronomical surveys to classify the outliers identified by the autoencoder, we are able to characterize over-densities in the t-SNE map. Our study specifically focuses on well-defined islands in the t-SNE space, corresponding to specific populations. We identified a large sample of white dwarfs and low-mass stars, including a small subset of polluted white dwarfs, and report potential candidates for spectroscopic follow-up, including 19 carbon-rich stars, 11 cataclysmic variables and 170 white-dwarfs-main-sequence binaries, all previously unreported in the literature.

papers.title: Controlling Optical Quantum Interference with Plasmonic Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. Here, we tackle this problem by presenting a composite quantum plasmonic metasurface operating as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter capable of achieving both single photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference just by varying the incident photons frequency or changing the design dimensions. The presented metasurface combines a plasmonic grating corrugated by periodic nanoslits that can achieve extraordinary optical transmission with additional nanostripes on top forming nanocavities characterized by localized gap plasmon resonances. The photon-photon interactions are analyzed based on calculating the quantum coalescence metric which accurately portrays the obtained bunching or anti-bunching quantum interference. The presented quantum interference operation is applicable to both fundamental non-classical light interactions and in the design of more applied quantum optical logic gates used in quantum computing and communications.

papers.title: Learning Parameters of dRGT Black Holes in Nonlinear Electrodynamics with Neural Network Scenarios
papers.abstract: Using machine learning methods, we present constraining parameter scenarios of AdS black holes in dRGT-like massive gravity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics. We first approach the photon sphere, the black hole shadow, and the energy emission rate with the help of high performance parallel computations. To corroborate such optical results, we develop a numerical framework to constrain the electric charge and the nonlinear electrodynamic parameter, for certain gravity regimes, via the shadow observations reported by the Even Horizon Telescope collaboration. Employing neural networks, we then examine the parameter regions of the black holes based on their consistency with EHT observations of M87$^*$, SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$, and SgrA$^*_{\mathrm{Keck}}$, within the $1-σ$ and $2-σ$ confidence intervals. As a result, we find that the obtained constraints are consistent with the $SgrA^*_{\mathrm{VLTI}}$ empirical data.

papers.title: Sionna Bench: Towards Benchmarks in Wireless Communications
papers.abstract: Academic research in wireless communications has no tradition of benchmarks so far. Remarkable progress in benchmark-oriented fields like machine learning suggests that the adoption of benchmarks could benefit our field. In the absence of benchmarks, however, a scientific debt has accumulated: since the academic community has not canonized specific problem setups, methods that address essentially the same problem were often developed for slightly different setups and lack a common framework for comparison. Any attempt to establish a new benchmark is faced with the challenge of resolving this debt. Recent advances in agentic artificial intelligence (AI) create an opportunity to do so by leveraging AI-assisted coding. This makes it possible to implement the state-of-the art at scale and to adapt it to a common framework for comparison. We present Sionna Bench to initiate benchmarks in academic wireless communications research. As a pilot study, we use the problem of MIMO-OFDM channel estimation. At the time of writing, Sionna Bench's channel estimation benchmark features twenty channel estimation methods that were implemented from ten different papers. The ability to compare methods against the state-of-the-art will be crucial for navigating the research landscape in an era where AI-generated methods coexist with human-developed algorithms.

papers.title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
papers.abstract: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. The proposed model leverages TFT to learn short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance, while N-BEATS captures long-term trend and seasonal components through interpretable basis decomposition. An adaptive attention mechanism dynamically fuses both branches, enabling balanced multi-scale learning. The framework simultaneously generates forecasts for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour horizons within a single unified pipeline. The model is evaluated using multi-year real-world datasets from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11 across the 20162017, 2023, 2024, and 20252026 datasets, respectively, corresponding to a 3540% reduction compared to the best baseline (TFT). Additionally, MAPE remains below 5% across all datasets, indicating high predictive accuracy and stability. The model also provides interpretability through attention visualization and trendseasonality decomposition, and is deployed on a cloud-based platform for real-time forecasting. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is robust, interpretable, and suitable for practical renewable energy applications.

papers.title: Cross-disorder Learning of Imaging-derived Joint Mophometric Markers in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Diseases
papers.abstract: As two most prevalent neurodegenerative diseases (NDDs), Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD) shared commonalities both in symptomology and pathophysiology. However, to what extent and in what way these two distinct disorders overlap remain underexplored. In this study, we propose an explicit, interpretable and spatially adaptive transfer learning framework to elucidate the morphometric biomarkers linked to AD and PD. We applied such high-dimensional machine learning model to two most popular open-source neuroimaging datasets, i.e., Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) and Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI). On the one hand, our cross-disorder classifier revealed neuro-anatomical alteration patterns well aligning with previous neuroimaging research findings and underscoring patients' clinical presentations. On the other hand, the spatially adaptive trained classifier using shared prior achieved statistically superior diagnostic performance compared to respective individual models, which further highlights the cross-disorder framework's efficacy on modeling limited-size datasets across disease domains.

papers.title: Towards Interaction State Recognition in Sensorized Gecko-Inspired Adhesive Interfaces for Orbital Servicing
papers.abstract: Reliable contact establishment remains a critical challenge for autonomous on-orbit servicing (OOS), particularly when interacting with non-cooperative targets. Gecko-inspired dry adhesives provide a lightweight, passive, and residue-free solution for robotic capture in space, yet current systems operate in open loop, without the ability to estimate their own contact or adhesion state during interaction. This paper presents a real-time interaction-awareness framework that enables sensorized gecko-inspired adhesive interfaces to estimate their contact state throughout the adhesion lifecycle using embedded capacitive sensing. Five discrete interaction states (idle, proximity, contact, engaged, and disengaged) are classified using experimentally collected and augmented sensor data, enabling a comparative evaluation of six lightweight machine learning models suitable for embedded deployment. Among the evaluated models, Random Forest achieved the highest offline classification accuracy of 95.65%. For online deployment, combining Random Forest with a rule-based state machine improved accuracy from 78.02% to 93.14%, achieving a macro F1-score of 0.9343 while maintaining a 53 ms inference cycle. These results demonstrate that incorporating physics-consistent state constraints significantly improves robustness during realtime inference, representing a step toward interaction-aware capture in future autonomous orbital servicing missions.

papers.title: Active isolation of transmon readout with a tunable inductive bridge
papers.abstract: Scalable superconducting quantum computation requires fast, high-fidelity readout. Currently, this is assisted through cryogenic amplification of the readout signal. In traditional dispersive readout schemes, the amplifiers that are used to provide high signal-to-noise ratio also generate thermal noise that can decohere the qubits, demanding additional ferrite-based isolators to suppress this noise. Here, we integrate a chip-scale microwave switch, the tunable inductive bridge, into the readout chain of a fixed-frequency transmon. Flux-pulsing the switch, such that it transmits only during the readout, did not make a discernable difference to qubit coherence, residual excited-state population, or readout fidelity metrics. By injecting broadband noise that mimics amplifier thermal photons, we show that the switch suppresses the resulting qubit dephasing by more than $30$~dB, consistent with its independently measured on-off ratio, establishing it as a potential chip-based integrated replacement for readout-chain isolators.

papers.title: Ammonia-Hydrogen Phase Equilibria in Planetary Envelopes from First-Principles-Based Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics
papers.abstract: Ammonia and hydrogen are major constituents of planets within and beyond the solar system, yet how they interact in planetary envelopes is poorly known. We perform large-scale two-phase coexistence simulations of the ammonia-hydrogen system from 500 to 4000 K and 0.1 to 100 GPa, driven by machine-learning interatomic potentials trained on density functional theory calculations. From these we map the compositions of coexisting hydrogen-rich and ammonia-rich phases, and the critical curve that separates conditions of complete miscibility from those of phase separation. The critical temperature increases with pressure, from 500 K at 0.1 GPa to 2000 K near 30 GPa, and we find no phase separation at 3000 and 4000 K up to 100 GPa. The slope of the critical curve decreases substantially between 0.3 and 30 GPa, and the curve nearly flattens above about 30 GPa and 2000 K, where molecules begin to give way to atomic species. The coexistence curves are asymmetric with an ammonia-rich critical composition. For the expected envelope compositions, the phase boundary lies close to, and intersects, published thermal profiles of Uranus and Neptune, implying ammonia may be raining out in these planets today. In contrast, in warm sub-Neptunes such as TOI-270 d, ammonia and hydrogen are likely miscible in all proportions. Together with previous studies, our results suggest that silicates, water and ammonia separate from hydrogen in sequence as planets cool, with implications for their compositional, thermal and structural evolution.

papers.title: Mind Your Boundaries: Boundary-Aware Model Obfuscation against Cross-node Attack
papers.abstract: With the advancement of powerful AI chips, on-device machine learning is gaining traction for its low latency and privacy protection. However, when edge devices are compromised, attackers can obtain white-box access to the deployed models by reversing the apps directly to obtain the knowledge of peer devices, which is known as Cross-Node Attacks, like performing efficient adversarial attacks. Most existing defenses target known vulnerabilities, yet white-box access still enables attackers to uncover more unknown weaknesses. This creates a critical risk for edge-device deployments, where one compromised device can endanger all models distributed from the same source. Motivated by findings that the model robustness is primarily influenced by the curvature of the decision boundary, we investigate how model parameters shape its curvature. In this paper, we propose a novel method, BMO, that obfuscates model parameters to diversify the decision boundary further resisting cross-node attack while preserving its benign accuracy. Specifically, we explore decomposing model parameters into boundary-position and boundary-curvature components based on null-space constraints, then models with differentiated decision boundaries are instantiated by injecting noise into the boundary-curvature component. Across all four major types of adversarial attacks with four widely-deployed on-device models, BMO achieves an average success rate of 68.68% in defense, far exceeding the most competitive baseline, which attains only 22.32% in defending against cross-node attacks. Moreover, BMO achieves comparable performance in benign accuracy compared with baselines.

papers.title: ASTROLABE: A 3D Particle-Level Surrogate for Cosmology Simulation with Physical Flow Matching
papers.abstract: The microphysics of dark matter (DM) is imprinted on cosmological structure across an enormous dynamic range. Nonlinear cosmological observables are most reliably modeled with N-body and hydrodynamic simulations. However, systematic N-body scans over DM theory space are prohibitively expensive. Machine learning emulators provide a possible solution, but are currently limited by either low resolution or only the ability to emulate specific observables. We introduce Astrolabe, a flow-matching-based generative emulator designed to be free of both constraints. Astrolabe acts directly on the 6N phase-space coordinates of N individual particles. With no voxel grid in the output, there is no voxel-resolution ceiling, and in principle any observable can be measured from inference. Astrolabe is computationally tractable via a field-particle hybrid transformer in which every particle cross-attends to multiscale field tokens, so compute and memory are linear in N. Astrolabe incorporates physical flow matching by taking the prior distribution for the flow to be approximate COmoving Lagrangian Acceleration (COLA)-based coordinates rather than unphysical noise, with momentum and mass conservation enforced at all points along flow time. In the Lambda-CDM cases we test, Astrolabe produces realistic fields with accurate power spectra, halo mass functions, velocity profiles, and halo density profiles. We also observe out-of-distribution generalization, with accurate emulation of dark-acoustic oscillation initial conditions. Astrolabe is also capable of being fine-tuned to simulate very large N and we demonstrate this by emulating a TNG50-3-dark simulation at a fraction of the cost.This method represents a first step toward a general and powerful cosmology simulation surrogate, which may eventually permit the inclusion of baryonic physics and a systematic exploration of richer dark sector interactions.

papers.title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity
papers.abstract: Bilevel optimization provides a framework for machine learning tasks such as hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning. Existing Newton-based bilevel methods typically rely on the classical hypergradient formula, which is generally unavailable when lower-level solutions are nonunique and the lower-level Hessian is singular. We develop two Newton-based methods beyond lower-level strong convexity by exploiting curvature shared by the lower-level and multiplier updates. Newton-based GALET handles potentially singular lower-level curvature under a positive spectral-gap condition, exploiting its range structure to avoid the squared-Hessian multiplier system used in GALET. Newton-based BAMM uses a strongly convex aggregation model when the lower-level objective is convex and the upper-level objective is strongly convex in the lower-level variable. We establish convergence guarantees and improved complexity bounds relative to GALET and sl-BAMM under the corresponding assumptions. We further introduce GNBO, a generalized Newton-based framework that captures the shared-curvature structure of the proposed methods and several existing Newton and quasi-Newton bilevel methods. Experiments on synthetic problems, data hyper-cleaning, and GPT-2 data reweighting evaluate the proposed methods across different bilevel learning tasks.

papers.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum Hamiltonian Embeddings
papers.abstract: Machine learning is widely regarded as a promising application in which quantum computing could offer a computational advantage. However, general quantum machine learning models with provable guarantees on performance, trainability, and efficient inference remain limited. In this work, we introduce quantum Hamiltonian embeddings, a supervised learning framework in which a classical training dataset is encoded into a single effective, parameterized Hamiltonian. Training optimizes the parameters of this data-dependent Hamiltonian, whose approximate ground state defines the classification rule. Once the ground state has been approximated using a quantum algorithm, inference can be performed either classically using a classical representation of the learned state, or with a quantum representation of the state. We establish efficient methods for gradient estimation and prove favorable generalization guarantees. Furthermore, under standard cryptographic assumptions, we show that Hamiltonian embeddings can realize hypothesis functions beyond the reach of efficient classical algorithms. We then demonstrate the framework at scale on IBM Heron processors using a standard benchmark dataset. Together, these results establish Hamiltonian embeddings as a new framework for quantum machine learning, combining theoretical guarantees with a path for experimental investigations at scale on quantum hardware.

papers.title: On Data Scaling in Tabular ML: More Data, Better Generalization?
papers.abstract: Recent work in tabular machine learning has emphasized the importance of diverse and realistic evaluation settings. The niche of large-scale (1M+) data, however, remains under-explored. To study training-data scaling, we assemble eight real-world tabular datasets with up to around ten million training examples, retaining the natural distribution shifts of the tasks and using random-split evaluation as a control. We find that GBDTs and MLP-based models show broadly similar scaling trends, with gains from both additional training data and algorithmic improvements. Tabular foundation models show more varied scaling behavior, with recent versions benefiting more consistently from larger contexts even under distribution shift. However, scaling training data under distribution shift introduces new challenges: in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance mostly improve together at smaller scales but can diverge at larger scales. We examine this through MLP capacity sweeps and comparisons of the validation distributions used for tuning and early stopping in MLPs and GBDTs. We also compare common practices of using validation data, contrasting its use for model selection in MLP pipelines with using it for in-context fitting in tabular foundation model pipelines. Under stronger shifts, MLPs selected using validation representative of the evaluation conditions generally maintain or improve performance as training data grows. In contrast, including such examples in context improves foundation-model performance, but does not prevent deterioration with increasing training size in our experiments.

papers.title: Training with ML-labeled Data via Stochastic First- and Zeroth-Order Optimization
papers.abstract: Training a machine learning (ML) model is an optimization process that typically requires a set of examples with ground-truth labels beforehand. Obtaining these ground truths usually requires laborious human effort and can be costly. The scalability of human labeling becomes a concern when there are a large number of data points that need to be labeled. To address this practical issue, we consider an optimization setting where a subset of samples has ground-truth labels, while the remaining data points were labeled by an ML predictor, which could potentially assign incorrect labels to those points. We propose both first-order and zeroth-order stochastic optimization methods for training on datasets consisting of a mix of true-labeled and ML-labeled samples. We further conduct comprehensive empirical studies from training a linear regression model to fine-tuning a large language model (LLM) to showcase the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms for training with ML-labeled data.

papers.title: MOFFieldBench: A Machine Learning Benchmark for Continuous Electronic Fields in Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) predominantly rely on atomic structures, whereas electron-density (ED) and electrostatic-potential (ESP) fields remain underexplored as scalable learning representations. These continuous fields encode complementary spatial and electronic information relevant to structure-property relationships, particularly pore geometry and guest-framework interactions, but costly first-principles calculations, storage requirements and the scarcity of systematically aligned datasets limit their broader use. Here we introduce MOFFieldBench, a multimodal benchmark comprising approximately 46,000 MOFs with one-to-one aligned crystallographic structures, ED fields and ESP fields. A unified workflow integrates field generation, error-controlled compression and sparse point-cloud representation, supporting field reconstruction, prediction of 13 material properties, multimodal property prediction and pairwise cross-modal retrieval. ED and ESP provide competitive representations for pore geometry, adsorption and separation properties. Multimodal fusion improves several prediction tasks relative to the best unimodal reference, supporting complementary predictive roles for atomic structures and electronic fields. Learned ED reconstruction closely approximates first-principles reference densities, while predicted-density initialization reduces self-consistent-field calculation time by 13.59\% on average in paired tests. These results support electronic fields as practical, informative learning modalities and establish MOFFieldBench as a resource for studying representation choice, multimodal learning and electronic-field-driven MOF modelling.

papers.title: Fluent but Fallible: Benchmarking Hallucination and Factual Reliability in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly advanced natural language processing and artificial intelligence applications through their capabilities in reasoning, text generation and knowledge retrieval. However, LLMs are still vulnerable to two important challenges: hallucination, generating factually incorrect or fabricated content, and response deviation, meaning systematic deviations from ground-truth responses. These limitations raise serious concerns regarding reliability and trustworthiness in academic and research environments. This study offers a thorough comparative analysis using a variety of metrics of ten advanced LLMs ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude~3.5~Sonnet, LLaMA~3, Mistral, Grok, Perplexity, DeepSeek~V3, Falcon, and Gemma based on a benchmark consisting of 70 carefully designed academic prompts across four complexity levels: Basic, Explanation, Advanced, and Tricky, evaluated in February 2025 on specific model versions. Each response was independently evaluated by three reviewers using five metrics: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, Response Deviation Index, and Hallucination Index. Perplexity and DeepSeek~V3 achieved the highest overall accuracy, while Gemini demonstrated strong recall and a well-balanced performance profile across all five metrics. LLaMA~3 showed strong resistance against hallucinations through a conservative method of generation. Advanced-level prompts proved most challenging across all models, while Tricky prompts were handled more reliably owing to their binary true/false structure. Falcon achieved perfect precision and zero hallucinations, but at the cost of the lowest recall and the highest response deviation. The results show a fundamental trade-off between response completeness and factual reliability, intensified by prompt complexity.

papers.title: Proof-of-Machine-Learning-Inference: Mining Knowledge, Not Hashes
papers.abstract: Bitcoin-style Proof-of-Work (PoW) secures permissionless blockchains but spends substantial computation on hash puzzles which have no utility other than extending the chain. At the same time, we have seen that the rise of generative AI has created significant demand for computational resources that are unfortunately available only to a few players. We propose a solution that solves both problems at the same time. In particular, we present Proof-of-ML-Inference (PoML), a consensus protocol in which miners perform user-requested machine-learning inference as part of their consensus algorithm. We identify exactly what computational assumptions are needed for ML inference to safely replace hash work, formalize those assumptions, and give evidence that LLMs and diffusion models satisfy them. We then formally analyse the security of our protocol by reducing the security of our protocol to the security of the Bitcoin Backbone model. Finally, we empirically evaluate block-time stability, showing that, in a simulated environment, PoML maintains a block production rate close to its calibrated block-time target.

papers.title: Doubly Robust Learning of Heterogeneous Survival Treatment Effects under Time-Varying Treatments
papers.abstract: Estimating heterogeneous survival treatment effects (HSTEs) from time-to-event data under time-varying treatments is important in fields such as medicine (e.g., to decide which sequence of treatments is better in terms of survival probability). However, this task is challenging because treatment decisions, patient characteristics, and censoring probability often evolve together, requiring sequential adjustment for both treatments and censoring. Existing survival learners mostly consider a single baseline treatment assignment, while longitudinal treatment-effect learners typically assume uncensored outcomes. In this paper, we introduce a novel doubly robust learner for heterogeneous survival treatment effects under time-varying treatments and history-dependent censoring. Our framework separates the intervention window from the survival horizon, with treatment prescribed for a finite period, after which care follows its natural course. We further establish the favorable theoretical properties of Neyman-orthogonality, rate double robustness and quasi-oracle efficiency. The framework accommodates flexible machine learning models for nuisance estimation and treatment-effect regression. We evaluate our learners through several numerical experiments, demonstrating their effectiveness.

papers.title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
papers.abstract: Foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise broad transferability, yet their out-of-domain reliability is hard to establish. Here, we use pure and O/H-containing disordered carbon spanning multiple phases, competing hybridisations and porous frameworks to stress-test six popular foundation MLIPs. We first screen all six on density functional theory (DFT) energy and force errors and binding curves, then subject four to melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics and evaluate the resulting structural observables. Binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories reveal unphysical extrapolation and dynamical failures that low DFT energy and force errors fail to reveal. Of the models tested, MACE-MH-1 is the most consistently robust, with low DFT errors and stable MD. Despite differing architectures, OMAT-based models share structural biases, highlighting the importance of training coverage. All four models generate structures of nanoporous carbon that reproduce the principal experimental and specialised carbon potential signatures. Incorporating O/H leaves short-range order largely unchanged but shifts pore-size distributions towards larger pores. These results emphasise the need for application-specific validation and extend molecular dynamics modelling of nanoporous carbon towards experimentally realistic structures.
